scope: Proved obstructions and lower bounds under their explicitly stated hypotheses. No global variable minimum or number-field counterexample is asserted.
origin: Historical theorem records separated from data/results.json, with additional proved obstruction records. The complete manuscript index is negative_results/README.md.

theorems.scope: Infinite input projections contained in O_K,S, for every number field K and finite S. The coordinate bounds also allow open conditions and finite alternatives. Individual-degree bounds concern essential coordinates of a single defining polynomial.
theorems.three_coordinate_system_theorem: The equations must have a common irreducible factor of total degree at least four.
theorems.nonnegative_scope: Globally nonnegative at one real embedding; includes all sums of squares. This does not exclude sign-changing quartics in three or four coordinates.
theorems.three_coordinate_quartic_constraints: Absolutely irreducible, dense smooth rational points, and sign-changing.

theorems.scope: No one unchanged existential formula defines rings of integers in every finite extension; a different formula for each field is not excluded.
Finite algebraic presentations of an infinite set of points of the specified elliptic curve over Q(sqrt(2)); not a general lower bound for defining Z.

For every number field F, no rational function A/B of two variables with max(deg A,deg B)<=3 is finite-to-one on the F-points of any nonempty archimedean open set. Some fiber there is infinite with unbounded height.
theorems.sharp_example: U^4-delta*V^4 for delta in F not a fourth power has finite F-fibers.
theorems.scope_limit: Ambient pairs only; not a lower bound on the coordinates of a Diophantine definition or on measurements of restricted elliptic multiples.

theorems.statement: Norm and trace graphs are Zariski dense in the affine plane over L, so have no quantifier-free definitions.
theorems.scope: Proper finite extensions of characteristic-zero fields; the obstruction concerns quantifier-free definitions, not existential definitions.

theorems.statement: Any fixed finite collection of existential formulas with infinite input projections over a number field simultaneously accepts some rational noninteger in a finite Galois extension of bounded degree.
theorems.scope_limit: No actual counterexample to a separately chosen defining polynomial for each field is established.

theorems.general_statement: For y^2=x^3+A*x+B over Q, if A,B are p-integral and B is a nonzero nonsquare modulo an odd prime p, every rational abscissa has even p-adic valuation.
theorems.example: E:y^2=x^3-2 has the infinite-order point (3,5), but 5 is not in the multiplicative subgroup generated by its rational abscissas.
theorems.scope_limit: This does not obstruct sums, more elaborate definitions, or definability of a ring of integers in its field.

theorems.statement: No q in Z[X] of degree at most two simultaneously reflects rational integrality, is odd at every integer, and has r(q(x)) square in Q_2 at every integer.
theorems.quadratic_classification: A*X^2+B*X+C with A nonzero reflects integrality if and only if |A| is squarefree and A divides B.
theorems.scope_limit: Only this odd-valued, uncorrected contact-square normalization; not corrected or parity-free routes and not a lower bound for arbitrary defining polynomials.

theorems.statement: In every listedQ(sqrt(d)), the projection is the same proper subsetD ofQ containing0,1 and excluding-1.
theorems.local_statement: D is simultaneously dense in every finite product ofQ-completions; every local input has witnesses in every completion of each listed quadratic field.
theorems.rank_verification: UnconditionalPARI ellrank bounds, with torsion and exact point calculations.
theorems.scope_limit: Not a definition ofZ,Q,or a ring of integers, and not a counterexample to existence of a different definition.

theorems.finite_presentation_bound: Recovering arbitrary tuples of r independent points in the specified simple Weil restriction by finite algebraic choices requires at least2r retained rational coordinates.
theorems.index_graph: For a Zariski-dense cyclic subgroup of an abelian variety, the graph {(n,[n]P)} is Zariski dense in G_a times that variety.
theorems.rational_curve_obstruction: The paired formal requirements H=[h]P at one split place and H-P at the other cannot hold for arbitrarily many good primes when E and P are rational.
theorems.two_curve_scope: A curve correspondence containing a common-index graph yields an isogeny and prevents infinitely many coprime reduction orders.
theorems.scope_limit: Restrictions on these specified compression mechanisms, not universal lower bounds for integer-defining polynomials.

large_prime_parity_counterexample.scope: These congruences alone; the full Gaussian-generator and avoidance conditions are not asserted.

theorems.statement: Every finite union of fixed rational-function images on finite products of fixed abelian varieties over a number field, even with finitely many values added, misses infinitely many rational integers.
theorems.source: Corvaja and Zannier, arXiv:2608.28255v1, Theorem1.1; Mordell-Weil finite generation.
theorems.consequence: Finite rational operations on the specified stable-elliptic subsets cannot produce a set containing every integer.
theorems.scope_limit: Does not cover arbitrary algebraic correspondences or unrestricted affine witnesses. Not a nondefinability theorem for rings of integers.

theorems.statement: The projection in each specified quadratic field is zero together with ratios of nonzero rational elliptic slopes; it misses infinitely many rational integers.
theorems.scope_limit: Not a definition of the rational subfield or a ring of integers. The bounded search does not certify particular omitted values.

theorems.statement: For a variety mapping to an abelian variety, if each geometric fiber has only finitely many output values, its rational outputs meet every finitely generated multiplicative subgroup in a finite set.
theorems.includes: Quasi-finite covers and affine translates of multiplicative subgroups; generic finiteness alone requires exceptional fibers to be treated separately.

theorems.statement: Over an abelian base, bounded-denominator outputs with soluble unirational fibers or smooth proper genus-one fibers equipped with an ample line bundle cannot cover all integers.
genus_one_inputs: finite map to the relative Jacobian
theorems.scope_limit: No obstruction for all higher-genus families, and no counterexample to general ring-of-integers definability.

theorems.statement: No fixed rational value of the parameter e gives the complete stated zero-preparation pole certificate.
theorems.scope_limit: These counterexamples range over prepared inputs. They do not exclude a fixed retained parameter on a specially selected prime-pattern subfamily.
theorems.dense_prepared_counterexamples: For tau=+/-17, counterexamples are dense in every real subinterval of (0,17), with valuations4,2,2 at2,3,17.

theorems.statement: Two explicit prepared inputs cannot share an actual pole parameter; symmetric contact products can have odd radical one at unbounded scale height.
theorems.scope_limit: Obstructions to specified simplifications, not general coordinate lower bounds.

theorems.statement: The natural even-power Frey family has exponential growth of the reduced j denominator in logarithmic height. Infinitely many required integer witnesses fail the fixed asymmetric-size hypotheses.
theorems.frey_denominator_lower_bound: max(|A|,|B|)^(4*d)/256 for coprime nonzero A,B and positive even d
theorems.scope_limit: Applicability obstruction for the specified families; neither disproves abc nor excludes other families.

theorems.statement: For every rational a>4, lambda=-(a+1)/(5a) gives a negative nonzero square R(lambda)R(a*lambda), hence odd radical one. This applies to the source scales a=beta^8+T(n)^8. Positive unbounded-scale examples and the full twelve-element contact automorphism group are also proved.
theorems.scope_limit: The fixed product alone cannot support a uniform height bound. These examples do not satisfy all the other elliptic and pole constraints automatically; no counterexample to the 13-variable theorem is claimed.

theorems.scope: For every number field K with i not in K and every D in K*, with E_D:y^2=x^3-D*x and L=K(i).
theorems.trace_statement: For a nontorsion P in E_D(K), C=(1+iota)P has Tr_L/K x([n]C)=Tr_L/Q x([n]C)=0 for all nonzero n, while h(x([n]C))=4*n^2*hat_h(P)+O_E(1).
theorems.sum_statement: The four distinct doubled points [2n]P, iota[2n]P, [4n]P, iota[4n]P have distinct abscissas summing to zero and unbounded heights.
theorems.explicit_nontorsion_certificate: Reduction orders5 and3 at primes17 and23; group orders20 and24 exclude torsion.
theorems.scope_limit: An obstruction to extending the particular elliptic group and height mechanism; no counterexample to Diophantine definability of O_L in L is claimed.

theorems.fixed_parameters: Odd integer B>=3, nonzero integer n, rational T>6; beta(X)=2*X^2+B; a(X)=beta(X)^8+T^8.
theorems.statement: For every nonzero Psi in Q(X,lambda), there are a fixed positive cone of contact depths, a nonzero parity class, and infinitely many good primes such that every positive depth pair in that cone and parity class is realized by half-integral X and lambda=s^2+t^2>1 with integers s,t. The two contact values have those depths, Psi is defined and nonzero with even valuation, and beta(X)-n is a p-unit.
theorems.scope: No additional arithmetic conjecture; includes explicit rational dependence on the input and scale. The source specialization T=Tr(x([n]P)) is covered whenever T>6.
theorems.computation_scope: Two exact illustrative examples, independently checked by BigInt integer arithmetic and Fraction rational arithmetic; the universal statement is a formal-series and prime-existence proof.
theorems.scope_limit: An obstruction to one rational function uniformly detecting the union of two odd contact valuations; no false solution of the complete Diophantine source and no absolute variable-count lower bound are asserted.
theorems.stronger_slope_restriction: The same conclusions hold with lambda=1+s^2 for a nonzero integer s; lambda-1 is an integer square.

theorems.finiteness: At each fixed scale and finite prime set, only finitely many admissible rational slopes have equal odd contact sets.
theorems.scope: Genus, finiteness and the inert-prime comparison obstruction are unconditional. The separately stated one-pole soundness implication retains weak abc and the original arithmetic premises; its converse is open. No new defining variable count.

theorems.statement: If ZP is Zariski dense in an abelian variety A, the triples ([n]P,[h]P,[nh]P) are Zariski dense in A^3 for any infinite set of n and any infinite set of h for each n.
theorems.elliptic_proof: An elementary intersection-degree argument using graphs of multiplication.
theorems.general_proof: Mordell-Lang gives a density criterion in terms of finite unions of rational affine hyperplanes in the index lattice.
theorems.consequence: No fixed algebraic correspondence with finite geometric fibers can recover the index product uniformly on those pairs; nonlinear polynomial index graphs satisfy the analogous obstruction.
theorems.scope: No claim about arbitrary Diophantine definitions, additional free parameters, positive-dimensional fibers with finite rational point sets, or specially selected finite sets of auxiliary indices.

theorems.statement: For the contacts {-1,0,2,3}, infinitely many rational t have unbounded logarithmic height and odd contact radical one outside {2,3,5}; the points can be chosen with 3<t<5.
theorems.proof_method: Exact birational transformations and a Nagell-Lutz nontorsion certificate give infinitely many rational points; the twist and contact differences bound the odd prime support.
theorems.scope: An obstruction to height bounds using this particular four-contact odd radical. It is not a nonintegral solution of a complete defining source, a counterexample to abc, or a variable-count lower bound.

theorems.statement: Prime assignments to consecutive integers alone do not control the odd radical; polynomial injections do not supply the finite algebraic recovery used in the elimination theorem.
theorems.scope: The paper distinguishes proved obstructions from the separately conditional implication of the connected-component conjecture; no formal nonimplication between RH, GRH, Grimm, and abc is claimed.

theorems.statement: The odd-valuation implication holds for y^2=T^2+kappa*R*(1+R*s^2)^2. For every m>=1, the prepared b_m=409*(204/1013^m)^2 gives no Q_1013-point on Y^2=1+b_m*(1+b_m*v^2)^2, including on its smooth projective model.
theorems.scope_limit: This disproves completeness on all prepared inputs even for a finite disjunction of fixed nonzero kappa values; the restricted comparison-prime family remains unresolved. No variable-count improvement follows.
theorems.general_obstruction: For every finite fixed set C of nonzero rational kappa, infinitely many prepared b tending to zero make all the corresponding smooth quartic curves locally insoluble at one prime.

theorems.statement: For H_j=[28101000+30510750j]P, j>=0, H_j reduces to O at (76537,sqrt(2)-26935) and H_j-P reduces to T0 at (76537,sqrt(2)-49602). All H_j belong to 2E(K) and satisfy the characteristic-zero reference-chart open conditions.
theorems.scope: Automatic agreement of torsion-translation signs cannot be deduced from the reference chart and doubling alone; no full detector counterexample is asserted.

theorems.statement: For nonzero C,D in characteristic zero, the pole surface with conic parameter variable resolves to a K3 surface. Its double-cover model has four A3 singularities. The component of a finite common-parameter product dominating the parameter line has no rationally connected smooth projective model.
theorems.scope: Fixed detector inputs only. No obstruction to rational points, common rational parameters, or constructions varying the auxiliary indices is asserted.

theorems.assumptions: C,D nonzero rational; tau transcendental; e=(tau^2-D)/(tau^2+3D).
theorems.affine_criterion: q^2=D(s^2-Ce)(s^2+3Ce) has s,q in Q(tau) iff C or -3D is a rational square.
theorems.projective_criterion: The smooth projective generic fiber has a Q(tau)-point iff at least one of C,D,-3D is a rational square.
theorems.prepared_criterion: For prepared b=d*a^2, D=17d and C=17(17-b), a section exists iff C is a rational square.
theorems.scope: A section obstruction, not nonexistence of specialized rational fibers, common rational parameters, multisections, or actual variable-input constructions.

theorems.statement: For every odd L>=3 in the original general source, some X in {3,6,7} has nonsquare-unit baseline complement modulo 23. Actual prepared guarded tuples and independent-index return families can keep all detector inputs in that nonsquare-complement neighborhood.
theorems.scope_limit: This excludes global square complements on those particular legitimate families, not on all source choices. It does not obstruct common rational fibers without sections.

theorems.statement: The original pole curves have no Q_409-point for any local conic parameter, whereas the normalized prepared input has a rational square complement and an explicit nonzero rational pole section. The square class is preserved.
theorems.scope_limit: A counterexample to replacing the final pole input by Phi(b), not a false solution of the complete detector source and not an objection to separately proved early-scalar changes.

theorems.statement: The stated squared reference factor admits exact cancellation at the specified split prime. Both whole-factor odd-cube repairs have local zeros, and arbitrarily high nonzero valuations, while the comparison error is a unit. The actual contact function has a local inverse realizing the required parameter.
theorems.scope_limit: Local factor-level implications only. No simultaneous global, cyclic, doubled, two-detector or full-source counterexample is asserted.

theorems.assumptions: Distinct positive rational D_i and fixed nonzero rational twist classes alpha_i; nonzero C_i for the full common-pole variety.
theorems.statement: Each fixed class tuple permits only finitely many rational parameters when r>=2. The rational-Mobius two-pole genus remains five when D_1/D_2 is nonsquare. A smooth proper model of the full common-pole variety has omega_X=f^*O(2r-2), hence Kodaira dimension one for r>=2 and cannot be birational to a finite quotient of an abelian variety.
theorems.scope_limit: No obstruction to one common rational fiber or the infinite union over varying classes. Direct Kummer-quotient methods are excluded for this variety, not every possible reformulation.

theorems.assumptions: Fixed source input and nonzero early scalar; an abelian parameter variety over Q; native point roles given by rational maps; all generic source guards nonzero; nonconstant detector argument.
theorems.statement: For the native ten-contact general and six-contact conditional detectors, the square complement is not a rational function-field square and the original normalized pole equations have no rational function-field witness, even with varying twist-class representative and all projective conic parameters.
theorems.proof_method: Q-simplicity of Res(E), codimension-two fibers of the reference map, an odd contact divisor forced by an etale-cover and higher-genus contradiction, and a universal negative-odd-valuation pole obstruction.
theorems.scope_limit: No exclusion of fixed-argument rational incidence lifts, individual arithmetic tuples, ramified covers, or all possible smaller Diophantine definitions. No 24-variable completeness theorem is established.

theorems.statement: The allowed global reference progression H_j=[10435875+61021500j]R0, P=2R0, has [2]H_j formal at the first place above 76537 and [2](H_j-P) in the T0 neighborhood at the other, producing opposite translation signs.
theorems.index_domain: All allowed source points, including half-integral indices relative to P.
theorems.scope_limit: The reference domain and admissible soundness contact primes do not ensure agreement of doubled signs. No complete detector or nonintegral defining-polynomial witness is asserted.

theorems.assumptions: Fixed allowed native input, slope, scales and root points, positive detector coefficient w, and the full independent auxiliary product (Res E)^5 or (Res E)^2 with generic source guards.
theorems.statement: The square-complement double cover is geometrically ramified. It cannot acquire a rational section under a surjective translated homomorphism of abelian varieties, including all isogenies and the independent half-point doubling map.
theorems.proof_method: Restriction to U_A^-=T0 leaves a moving elliptic function with pole divisor 4(T0+T++T−); only finitely many such functions can have an unramified normalized complement cover. Smooth surjective pullback preserves odd divisor multiplicities.
theorems.scope_limit: This is a uniform-section obstruction on the full product. It does not exclude proper lower-dimensional coupled subvarieties, individually chosen rational points, or common rational pole fibers without square complements. No new variable lower bound or 24-variable completeness theorem.

theorems.scope: Every finite set of nontrivial signed rational square classes for the original general scalar; arbitrary guarded rational source tuples and all nonzero rational m in levels17m^2; uniform in odd L.

theorems.sources: The original six-factor weak-abc and ordinary-abc native detectors
theorems.valuation_bound: v_p(Norm(W))<=-2*nu and v_p(a)<=-nu when v_p(w)=nu>0 is odd outside S
theorems.auxiliary_scope: Every guarded tuple; split and inert primes; no square-norm assumption
theorems.finiteness_method: Finite exceptional square classes and Faltings on genus-two twists of the six-contact polynomial
theorems.consequence: Finitely many integer inputs for fixed B; no rational input for sufficiently large B; fixed finite rational rescalings do not repair uniform completeness
theorems.scope: The automatic-level method only. No obstruction to bounded norm levels, different scalars, individual compatible tuples, or all Diophantine definitions.

theorems.characteristic_zero_proof: Monic Laurent normal forms lift the certified modular ranks; explicit spanning identities vanish on the entire false family
theorems.consequence: Every quadratic identity of the specified embedding, including rational conjugate products and the physical trace, vanishes on a false tangent family with arbitrary trace
theorems.scope: No statement about different embeddings, additional helpers, identities required only on a restricted arithmetic family, or a global variable minimum.

theorems.statement: Every fixed finite set of affine identifications S=[m]A+[k]P excludes an infinite arithmetic progression of integer inputs in the specified general source.
theorems.scope: Original beta=216X^4+450459 and scalar rho, throughout the sufficiently large coefficient range where n=beta. All original guards and arithmetic premises retained.

conditional_source.all_slope_scope: Actual prepared tuples with source shift B>=19; only simultaneous unit trace is excluded.

The q0=0 one-coordinate specialization on prepared inputs; no assertion that the input is an actual detector tuple.
